answer: A memory-bound protocol curbs Sybil attacks by challenging agents to traverse uncacheable tables in local RAM within microsecond limits. Verifiers evaluate access times along a latency ridge, raising a saffron alert if concurrent fetches clash. Because pseudorandom pointers branch like wild yarrow across physical memory banks, an attacker incurs the scarce cost of dedicated DRAM channels per identity. However, noisy virtualized neighbors can trigger false rejections.
